one_line: Nvidia reinstates Huang, U.S. targets Megaspeed, and AI agents expand into coding, security, and chip attacks.

themes.title: U.S. chip policy and Nvidia leadership
themes.text: Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO and board chair less than two weeks after his resignation, following discussions with senior U.S. government officials. Separately, the Commerce Department plans to add Singapore-based Megaspeed to the Entity List, requiring licenses for chip sales after investigations into alleged Nvidia export violations.

stories.headline: Nvidia board reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO and board chair
U.S. Commerce Department to add Megaspeed to Entity List, restricting chip sales

themes.title: AI agents expand into coding and security
themes.text: Anthropic launched Claude Ship to auto-review and approve GitHub pull requests, Google DeepMind detailed its AlphaEvolve coding agent, and OpenAI and Cisco released Shirudo, a runtime that blocked a Java4Shell exploit without a restart. Researchers also introduced ToolSmith, which auto-generates tool modules for multimodal search agents.

stories.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Ship to auto‑review and approve GitHub pull requests
Google DeepMind details AlphaEvolve coding agent
OpenAI and Cisco introduce Shirudo for Linux security
ToolSmith auto-generates tools for multimodal search agents

themes.title: Safety gaps draw attacks and lawsuits
themes.text: Radboud University demonstrated FATCAT, an electromagnetic fault-injection attack that disables safety refusals in Llama 3.2 and Gemma 3 models and causes hazardous robot movements. Meanwhile, Virginia and Oregon sued Musk companies alleging they stripped safeguards from Grok, enabling creation of child sexual abuse material and nonconsensual intimate imagery.

stories.headline: Researchers show physical chip attack can disable AI safety refusals
Virginia and Oregon sue Musk companies over Grok sexualized images

themes.title: India's AI industry moves
themes.text: Sarvam AI released an upgraded 105B model and a speech-to-text API supporting 22 Indian languages, while defending its hosting of Chinese open-weight models. Nasscom proposed a three-year AI scheme for Indian IT firms in Budget 2027-28, and a Systematix report said AI adoption will sustain demand for Indian IT services even as it pressures labor-based delivery models.

stories.headline: Sarvam defends hosting Chinese models, releases upgraded 105B model
Sarvam AI launches Dictate API for English and 22 Indian languages
Nasscom proposes three-year AI scheme for Indian IT firms in Budget 2027-28
Systematix report: AI adoption to sustain Indian IT services demand, labor models pressured
